questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Difficult. It was a constant load of information, but not the kind you actually needed. It was so messy with all the portals and system not being related or able to "communicate". You never knew what to do, or where to find information. This was just as much the Danish system as the English.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A group of kind exchange students that was just as confused as me, and we helped each other to find the necessary information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its way better to live close to the city, than isolated at campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I went to the IT 4-5 times. They were nice, but it was all so confusing

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had a solid help from Phillip, who sat up a meeting ith the pharmacies students and introduced us well, and talked us through the courses they could offer.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply with a friend from Denmark, so you have two confused brain cells instead of one. Ask questions, it often helped.
